title: Auto-Hide Panel elements that only requires hovering can still be triggered and interacted with while it's hidden by dragging and dropping desktop items underneath the Panel's hitboxes
line: Dropping a desktop file where a hidden auto-hide panel would be no longer pops up that panel's tooltips.
explanation: When a drag ends on Wayland, Qt synthesizes a button release without a window, and QGuiApplication delivers it (plus a synthetic move) to whichever top-level window it thinks is under the cursor. Qt doesn't know KWin has hidden the auto-hide panel, so the hidden panel got that move and release, its Qt Quick scene registered hover there and tooltips such as the task manager's opened next to the invisible panel. PanelView now ignores mouse events on an auto-hide or dodge-windows panel that the pointer hasn't entered; real use always sends an Enter first, so the revealed panel behaves as before.

commits.message:
shell: ignore mouse events that reach a hidden auto-hide panel

At the end of a drag, Qt sends a button release that has no window to
the top-level window under the cursor, which can be a hidden panel, so
its tooltips opened. Now such a panel ignores them unless entered.

BUG: 514219

patches.diff:
From 3431d3c74b36ebdac96775ca4e38c606efb13d52 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:28:23 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] shell: ignore mouse events that reach a hidden auto-hide
 panel

At the end of a drag, Qt sends a button release that has no window to
the top-level window under the cursor, which can be a hidden panel, so
its tooltips opened. Now such a panel ignores them unless entered.

BUG: 514219
---
 shell/panelview.cpp | 7 +++++++
 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+)

diff --git a/shell/panelview.cpp b/shell/panelview.cpp
index 5c0ac43e71..307dc5a8fe 100644
--- a/shell/panelview.cpp
+++ b/shell/panelview.cpp
@@ -1197,6 +1197,13 @@ bool PanelView::event(QEvent *e)
     case QEvent::MouseButtonDblClick: {
         auto *me = static_cast<QMouseEvent *>(e);
 
+        // Qt can route a mouse event that has no window, like the release synthesized at the end of a drag,
+        // to a hidden panel. A panel the pointer never entered must not react to it.
+        if (edgeActivated() && !m_containsMouse && !m_fakeEventPending) {
+            e->accept();
+            return true;
+        }
+
         // first, don't mess with position if the cursor is actually outside the view:
         // somebody is doing a click and drag that must not break when the cursor i outside
         // BUG 482580: use QRectF for HiDPI
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Pure master, left auto-hide panel hidden: after dropping dragme.txt where the panel's Chrome launcher is and keeping the pointer still, the 'Google Chrome' tooltip appears next to the invisible panel
Same drop with the fix: no tooltip, the panel stays hidden (0 of 6 tries)

review.text: The root cause is QtWayland (a window-less release after a drag routed via topLevelAt), so a Plasma-side guard is reasonable, but this one is too broad. It swallows every mouse event on any AutoHide/DodgeWindows panel that has no Enter, including a visible Dodge-Windows panel, and mouse events Qt synthesizes from tablet/pen input, which may come without a QEvent::Enter. The 1/4 vs 0/6 repro is thin, though the log line confirms that the hidden panel receives the stray events.
changes: Only drop the events while the panel is actually hidden by auto-hide (e.g. the autohide screen edge is active), not whenever m_containsMouse is false
Test pen/tablet input on a revealed auto-hide panel, and dragging a task/launcher out of a revealed auto-hide panel (no stuck pressed state)
Report the QtWayland bug upstream and reference it in a comment
